questions.question: Which finding most strongly supports acne vulgaris rather than papulopustular rosacea?
choices: Open and closed comedones
Persistent facial flushing without comedones
Ocular burning and telangiectasias
Papules limited to the central face after heat exposure
questions.explanation: Comedones are a defining clue for acne vulgaris. Rosacea often has central erythema, flushing, papules, or pustules but typically lacks comedones.

questions.question: Why should a patient with deep acne nodules and early scars receive prompt escalation rather than serial over-the-counter trials?
choices: Scarring and psychosocial burden make disease clinically severe even if lesion count is modest
All acne resolves within one week
Nodules are never inflammatory
Only cosmetic outcomes matter
questions.explanation: Painful nodules and scarring can lead to permanent harm and major distress. Severity includes lesion depth, scars, distribution, function, and mental-health impact.

questions.question: What is an antimicrobial-stewardship principle for inflammatory acne?
choices: Use oral antibiotics indefinitely as monotherapy
When antibiotics are used, combine appropriately with nonantibiotic topical therapy and reassess duration
Avoid all topical therapies
Start multiple antibiotics without confirming the diagnosis
questions.explanation: Antibiotics should not be continued indefinitely without reassessment. Combining with agents such as benzoyl peroxide when appropriate can help reduce resistance pressure and treat multiple acne mechanisms.

questions.question: Which review is essential before selecting many acne medications?
choices: Pregnancy potential and current pregnancy status
Preferred topical vehicle without considering medication safety
Whether a topical antibiotic alone should be used indefinitely for every acne pattern
Family history of seasonal allergic rhinitis only
questions.explanation: Reproductive safety changes medication choices. Pregnancy potential should be assessed respectfully and incorporated into treatment and referral planning.

questions.question: Which symptom in a patient with rosacea warrants a lower threshold for prompt eye-care evaluation?
choices: Eye pain, photophobia, or reduced vision
A single stable comedone
Mild seasonal dry skin alone
A healed acne scar
questions.explanation: Ocular rosacea or another eye process can cause significant symptoms. Eye pain, light sensitivity, or visual change requires timely evaluation rather than routine skin follow-up.

questions.question: Which pattern most strongly suggests hidradenitis suppurativa?
choices: Recurrent painful nodules, drainage, tunnels, and scars in axillae or groin
A few isolated comedones on the forehead
A single brief allergic rash on the wrist
A painless stable nevus
questions.explanation: HS is chronic inflammatory follicular disease characterized by recurrent deep lesions, drainage, tunnels, and scarring in characteristic intertriginous locations.

questions.question: What is the most appropriate way to discuss hidradenitis suppurativa with a patient?
choices: Frame it as a hygiene failure
Use nonjudgmental language and assess pain, drainage, function, mood, and access to care
Tell the patient to scrub lesions aggressively
Avoid discussing sensitive sites
questions.explanation: HS is not caused by poor hygiene. Trauma-informed, nonstigmatizing assessment improves diagnostic accuracy and supports treatment of pain, function, and psychological burden.

questions.question: A patient has an acute fluctuant painful HS-region collection with fever and spreading redness. What is the priority?
choices: Assess for systemic infection and arrange urgent care with drainage or surgical capability as indicated
Delay evaluation until a dermatology visit months later
Only recommend cosmetic products
Assume all drainage is noninfectious
questions.explanation: Systemic symptoms, rapidly spreading cellulitis, severe pain, or a fluctuant collection may require urgent infection assessment and source control, even in a patient with known HS.

questions.question: Why should FNP follow-up for acne, rosacea, or HS assess more than skin appearance?
choices: Visible disease cannot affect daily life
Pain, sleep, work, scarring, sexual health, mood, medication effects, and access influence outcomes
Follow-up is unnecessary after a prescription
Only lesion count affects treatment decisions
questions.explanation: These conditions can cause significant functional and psychosocial harm. Longitudinal care measures treatment response alongside quality of life, safety, and feasibility.

questions.question: Which reason most supports dermatology referral for acne?
choices: Nodulocystic disease, scarring, diagnostic uncertainty, or failure of a reasonable first-line plan
A patient asks how to wash their face
A single transient blemish after a mask
Stable mild disease controlled with a tolerated plan
questions.explanation: Scarring risk, severe inflammatory lesions, diagnostic uncertainty, and failure of appropriate initial treatment are reasons to refer early rather than wait for permanent damage.
